chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Muhammad al-Wabishi, who said:

Our companions were mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so I said, 'I do not have lunch nor dinner except that two or three of them, or fewer or more, are with me.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'Their merit upon you is greater than your merit upon them.'

I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! How is that, while I feed them my food, spend upon them from my wealth, and my dependents serve them?' He said, 'Indeed, when they come to you, they come with abundant sustenance from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and when they leave, they leave with forgiveness for you.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابُنَا: Our companions (referring to the righteous believers or scholars)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of hosting and feeding the righteous companions according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia concept of *Ihsan* (beneficence) as a reciprocal spiritual exchange rather than a one-sided charity. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the status of the *Mumin* by framing their presence as a conduit for divine sustenance (*rizq*) and forgiveness, shifting the host's focus from material expenditure to spiritual gain. This perspective reinforces the communal bond where serving the righteous is considered a means of attaining God's pleasure and mercy.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Muhammad Al Wabishy who said,

‘Our companions were mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I said, ‘I neither have lunch nor dinner except there are two of them with me, and the three, and less and more’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Their merit upon you is greater than your merit upon them’.

So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! How come and I am feeding them my food, and spending upon them from my wealth, and my dependants are serving them?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They, when they come over to you, enter with a lot of sustenance from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, and when they exit, they go out with the Forgiveness for you’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Muhammad al-Wabishi who has said the following:

“Our people were mentioned before abu ‘Abd Allah, recipient of divine supreme covenant. I said, ‘I do not eat lunch or dinner without two, three or more or less of them with me.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) said, ‘Their merit over you is greater than your merit over them.’

I then said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, how can it be as such? I feed them and spent for them from my property and my family serves them.’ The Imam said, ‘When they come to you they come with plenty of sustenance from Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, and when they leave, they do so with forgiveness for you.’”
